videos.title: Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game! Google's rumored Gemini 4 Krypton has sparked a massive question: did an unreleased AI model just prove it can build entire games? A leaked demo reportedly shows an eight-second anime-style animation generated entirely through code, taking 39 minutes and potentially involving nearly 247,000 tokens. But there's a major difference between generating impressive visuals and creating a playable game.

And that's where this story gets interesting.

On November 8, an X user known as Lyra claimed Google had developed an internal checkpoint called Krypton, reportedly outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. Another developer, Chetaslua, shared comparisons involving a model labeled "krypton-a," including a detailed PlayStation 4 controller rendered in SVG and an anime-style floating island animation.

The numbers are striking. According to the reported comparison, Krypton used approximately 22,000 thinking tokens to generate the controller, versus 4,000 for Carbon. The anime animation reportedly ran for 39 minutes and 16 seconds at roughly 105 tokens per second.

But none of this has been independently verified. Google hasn't officially announced Gemini 4 Krypton, published its benchmarks, confirmed its specifications, or provided a release date.

So what can these leaked demonstrations actually tell us?

We examine the origins of the Krypton name, the reported visual comparisons, the quarter-million-token calculation, and why producing an animation isn't equivalent to building an interactive game with player controls, collision detection, physics, and functioning gameplay systems.

Then we compare those rumors with something Google has already demonstrated: four Gemini 4 Argon AI agents working together inside Minecraft.

According to published research, the agents defeated the Ender Dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs and dying 605 times along the way. Unlike a short visual demo, this experiment involved extended planning, execution, failure, and recovery. But the agents were playing Minecraft through a programming interface, not building the game itself.

Google's official AI lineup makes the story even more interesting.

Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28 and expanded to more users November 10, focuses on difficult, long-horizon reasoning, software engineering, debugging, and complex workflows.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen, officially introduced November 12, takes a different approach: faster coding and agentic execution. Google lists a one-million-token unified context window and pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Alongside Hydrogen, Google introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity, allowing different models to handle different parts of a development workflow. Google reports that Orchestrator achieved task success close to Carbon while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

But how does Google's AI actually compare against OpenAI and Anthropic?

We examine the reported benchmark results, including Carbon's Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 59, compared with Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57.

The competition becomes more complicated on coding benchmarks. Carbon reportedly scores 61.2% on FrontierSWE 2, behind GPT-6 Astra's 65.5%, while leading on the cited Terminal-Bench 4.0 comparison with 65.2%.

These are different evaluations measuring different capabilities. None proves an AI can independently produce a polished, enjoyable game.

We also explore what OpenAI Codex, Anthropic's coding agents, and xAI's Grok game-generation demonstrations reveal about the growing competition in AI-assisted software development.

For game developers, the bigger question isn't whether AI can generate thousands of lines of code. It's whether AI agents can build, test, debug, and improve working interactive experiences reliably.

So did Gemini 4 Krypton actually build a game? Is Google testing a breakthrough coding model, or are viral demos creating expectations that the evidence doesn't support?

The distinction matters more than ever.

Subscribe to BitBiased for detailed coverage of Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, AI coding agents, cybersecurity, and emerging technology.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Did Gemini 4 Krypton Actually Build a Game?
01:19 Where the Krypton Name Actually Comes From

#Gemini4 #GoogleAI #GeminiKrypton #AIGameDevelopment #ArtificialIntelligence Google's rumored Gemini 4 Krypton has sparked a massive question: did an unreleased AI model just prove it can build entire games? A leaked demo reportedly shows an eight-second anime-style animation generated entirely through code, taking 39 minutes and potentially involving nearly 247,000 tokens. But there's a major difference between generating impressive visuals and creating a playable game.

And that's where this story gets interesting.

On November 8, an X user known as Lyra claimed Google had developed an internal checkpoint called Krypton, reportedly outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. Another developer, Chetaslua, shared comparisons involving a model labeled "krypton-a," including a detailed PlayStation 4 controller rendered in SVG and an anime-style floating island animation.

The numbers are striking. According to the reported comparison, Krypton used approximately 22,000 thinking tokens to generate the controller, versus 4,000 for Carbon. The anime animation reportedly ran for 39 minutes and 16 seconds at roughly 105 tokens per second.

But none of this has been independently verified. Google hasn't officially announced Gemini 4 Krypton, published its benchmarks, confirmed its specifications, or provided a release date.

So what can these leaked demonstrations actually tell us?

We examine the origins of the Krypton name, the reported visual comparisons, the quarter-million-token calculation, and why producing an animation isn't equivalent to building an interactive game with player controls, collision detection, physics, and functioning gameplay systems.

Then we compare those rumors with something Google has already demonstrated: four Gemini 4 Argon AI agents working together inside Minecraft.

According to published research, the agents defeated the Ender Dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs and dying 605 times along the way. Unlike a short visual demo, this experiment involved extended planning, execution, failure, and recovery. But the agents were playing Minecraft through a programming interface, not building the game itself.

Google's official AI lineup makes the story even more interesting.

Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28 and expanded to more users November 10, focuses on difficult, long-horizon reasoning, software engineering, debugging, and complex workflows.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen, officially introduced November 12, takes a different approach: faster coding and agentic execution. Google lists a one-million-token unified context window and pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Alongside Hydrogen, Google introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity, allowing different models to handle different parts of a development workflow. Google reports that Orchestrator achieved task success close to Carbon while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

But how does Google's AI actually compare against OpenAI and Anthropic?

We examine the reported benchmark results, including Carbon's Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 59, compared with Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57.

The competition becomes more complicated on coding benchmarks. Carbon reportedly scores 61.2% on FrontierSWE 2, behind GPT-6 Astra's 65.5%, while leading on the cited Terminal-Bench 4.0 comparison with 65.2%.

These are different evaluations measuring different capabilities. None proves an AI can independently produce a polished, enjoyable game.

We also explore what OpenAI Codex, Anthropic's coding agents, and xAI's Grok game-generation demonstrations reveal about the growing competition in AI-assisted software development.

For game developers, the bigger question isn't whether AI can generate thousands of lines of code. It's whether AI agents can build, test, debug, and improve working interactive experiences reliably.

So did Gemini 4 Krypton actually build a game? Is Google testing a breakthrough coding model, or are viral demos creating expectations that the evidence doesn't support?

The distinction matters more than ever.

videos.summary_source_text:
How To Avoid Losing Muscles After 40? From your forties on, your body starts taking muscle from you, starting with your legs. It doesn't hurt and it gives no warning. Grip strength predicts the risk of dying better than blood pressure, yet fewer than 1 in 3 adults do the one thing that brings muscle back.

This documentary covers what the research shows about muscle loss after 40, why it matters, the 1990 Boston study that changed the field, and the three mistakes most people over 40 make.

Education, not a diagnosis. Talk to your doctor before starting a new training program.

videos.title: This Fixes 95% of Posture Problems (FAST!)
videos.summary_source_text:
This Fixes 95% of Posture Problems (FAST!) If you want to learn how to fix bad posture in 22 days, this step by step video gives you a plan for improving posture with stretches and strengthening exercises. Instead of guessing which posture exercises you need, I’m going to show you six simple tests you can perform at home to identify areas that need attention. Then, I’ll show you the stretches and exercises to address them and build your own posture correction routine.

Workouts, supplements, and mealplans here - http://athleanx.com
Subscribe to this channel here - http://youtube.com/user/jdcav24

The key to better posture is addressing your specific limitations consistently. This 22 day posture routine starts with testing your movement so you can focus on the areas that need work.

How to fix bad posture:

Day one starts with the posture test. As a physical therapist, I recommend seeing a qualified professional for an individual evaluation to understand your posture, the severity of any limitations and differences between your left and right sides. The six tests in this video give you a starting point for identifying areas to work on at home.

We’re looking at six areas: thoracic spine mobility, hamstring flexibility, calf flexibility, abdominal flexibility, hip flexor mobility and hip rotation. A rounded upper back, tight hamstrings, tight calves, tight abs, tight hip flexors and limited hip rotation can all affect how you move. Testing each area helps you decide which mobility exercises and stretches belong in your routine.

Each test uses a pass or fail approach. If you pass a test, you can skip the corresponding correction in this plan. If you fail a test, include the stretches and strengthening exercises shown for that area. This keeps your posture workout focused on your results instead of having you perform every exercise whether you need it or not.

After your initial assessment, alternate stretching days with exercise or strengthening days for the next 20 days. Follow the recommended hold times, sets and reps demonstrated in the video for each of your selected corrections. On day 22, repeat the original tests to see where your mobility and control have improved and what still needs attention.

For example, if your upper back is rounded and you struggle to extend through your thoracic spine, start with the kneeling thoracic extension stretch. Place your elbows on a surface in front of you, lower your chest and gently move your upper back into extension. The goal is to work on upper back mobility with control rather than force yourself into a position you cannot comfortably reach.

On your strengthening days, the face pull works the muscles of the upper back and shoulders. When you’re looking for exercises for rounded shoulders or ways to improve upper body posture, it’s easy to focus only on stretching. This routine pairs mobility work with strengthening so you also train the muscles that help you control your position.

The same approach applies to the other areas you test. Tight hip flexors, limited hip rotation or tight hamstrings may call for different corrections, which is why the assessment comes first. Use the demonstrations to choose your exercises for bad posture, and follow the instructions instead of adding random stretches to your day.

Improving posture takes consistency. You didn’t develop your everyday movement habits in a single day, and one posture stretch is not going to change everything overnight. Treat these 22 days as an opportunity to establish a repeatable routine, measure your progress and learn which areas deserve more attention.

You also don’t want to overdo the stretching. More force does not automatically mean better flexibility. Stay within a comfortable range, use controlled movement and avoid pushing through pain. The goal of these stretches for better posture is to gradually improve the movement you have available, not turn each session into a test of how much discomfort you can tolerate.

A useful posture correction routine combines flexibility, joint mobility and strength. Stretching addresses the restrictions identified by your tests, while the strengthening days help you practice controlling your movement. Keep following the schedule and use your final assessment to guide what you continue working on beyond day 22.

If you want to support better posture over the long term, complement this routine with a workout program that strengthens your entire body. The ATHLEAN-X programs combine strength training with attention to how you move. Head to athleanx.com and use the program selector to find the training plan that fits your goals.

For more videos on how to improve posture, stretches for tight muscles, upper back exercises and full body strength training, subscribe to the ATHLEAN-X YouTube channel. videos.title: The Reality of Reaching AGI
videos.summary_source_text:
The Reality of Reaching AGI Sam Altman says OpenAI will have an internal system it calls AGI by December 31, 2026. But does GPT-6 Astra actually meet OpenAI's own definition of artificial general intelligence? And with Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and xAI racing toward the same goal, which AI lab is genuinely closest?

Four CEOs have made four very different AGI predictions. Sam Altman has a deadline. Demis Hassabis sees AGI arriving within two to three years. Dario Amodei has put roughly 50/50 odds on a one-to-three-year timeline. And Elon Musk has reportedly suggested Grok 5 has around a 10% chance of achieving AGI.

But here's the problem: they aren't even using the same definition.

OpenAI's charter defines AGI as highly autonomous AI that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. Google DeepMind emphasizes the full cognitive range of the human brain. Anthropic focuses on transformative AI, while xAI sets its sights on answering fundamental questions about the universe.

So instead of trusting predictions, we're comparing the actual evidence.

Anthropic's newly released Fable 5.2 makes an even stronger case in some areas. It scores 74.6% on Terminal-Bench Science according to Anthropic, compared with Astra's 68.1%. Independent testing from Artificial Analysis puts Fable at 73%, supporting much of that result.

And then come Anthropic's extraordinary claims.

The company says approximately 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in just 30 hours. It reports AI-assisted advances in physics, protein design, and biological research. Anthropic also claims Claude now leads 26% of its internal AI research and development work.

But formalizing an existing proof isn't discovering new mathematics. Much of the scientific work still depends on human researchers, and several headline claims haven't been independently replicated.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon presents another challenge. Google's benchmarks show Argon winning 12 of 18 tests, including impressive results in video understanding and long-context reasoning. Yet limited availability makes broad independent verification difficult, and Google's comparisons predate Anthropic's latest release.

Meanwhile, Elon Musk's rumored AGI contender, Grok 5, hasn't launched. The available Grok 4.7 remains behind the leading models on independent intelligence rankings, despite xAI's enormous reported computing infrastructure.

But the biggest problem with every AGI prediction may be reliability.

METR's research estimates Anthropic's unreleased Mythos Preview can complete tasks requiring roughly 17.4 hours of human work at 50% success. Raise the reliability requirement to 80%, and that horizon drops to approximately three hours.

That's the difference between an impressive demonstration and an autonomous system you can actually depend on.

We also examine why AI benchmarks contradict each other, whether multi-agent systems are being mistaken for general intelligence, and why bigger GPU clusters alone may not determine the winner.

The missing pieces are substantial: reliable multi-day autonomy, continuous learning, long-term memory, real-world adaptability, and independently demonstrated recursive self-improvement.

So who leads the AGI race in late 2026?

Anthropic has compelling momentum in coding agents and AI-assisted science. OpenAI offers exceptional breadth in a publicly available flagship. Google leads in several multimodal and scientific areas. And xAI still has considerable ground to make up.

But none has publicly demonstrated AGI under OpenAI's own charter definition.

The real question isn't whether OpenAI can announce AGI before December 31. It's whether the company can provide evidence that independent researchers can actually verify.

Watch the full breakdown to see which lab has the strongest case, which benchmarks matter, and what breakthrough could completely change the AGI race.

Subscribe to BitBiased for evidence-driven coverage of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, AI breakthroughs, cybersecurity, and emerging technology.

videos.title: How To Swing Slower And Still Gain Distance With Driver
videos.summary_source_text:
How To Swing Slower And Still Gain Distance With Driver Want to know how to hit longer drives without maxing out your swing speed driver training? In this golf lesson, you’ll learn simple setup and strike tweaks for better golf drives that add instant carry distance—even if you swing slower.

Most amateur golfers lose 20+ yards off the tee not because they lack clubhead speed, but because they hit down on the ball with a low launch angle and too much backspin. By adjusting your tee height, spine tilt, and impact focus, you can optimize your launch window and even build in an effortless draw.

In this video, you will learn:

Why teeing the ball higher increases your Angle of Attack (AoA) and carry distance
The simple "Right-Hand Setup Drill" to lock in the ideal driver spine tilt
Where to strike the ball on the clubface to reduce distance-killing spin
The "Ball Logo Trick" to stop lunging forward on your downswing
How to fix the pull/left miss that happens when you start hitting up on the driver

0:00 How to swing slower and hit your driver further
0:26 Step 1: Why tee height controls your launch angle & distance

Pulls, fades, poor contact and drives that come up short often start with the left side of your body: a level setup, an all-arms backswing with no width, and a left shoulder that moves too far forward on the way down. That leaves you hitting down on the ball with no speed, a pattern Eric Cogorno sees often in golf lessons with players who struggle with driver. The fix comes from what Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy and Justin Thomas have in common: a setup with your left hip and left shoulder higher, width in the backswing, and a left shoulder that goes up and back on the downswing. Together, these golf swing tips give you the two things Eric says you need to hit driver farther, an upward angle of attack and more speed, and he shows how to adjust the downswing feel for pulls and fades or pushes and hooks. If you leave this video without trying the feel of punching the club away from you, you're leaving speed and distance on the table.

• How to set up with your left hip and left shoulder higher

• How to create width like Bryson DeChambeau

• Why your left shoulder should go up and back, not forward, on the downswing
• How to fix pulls and fades, or pushes and hooks, with driver
• High handicap golf tips for golfers who struggle with driver

PGA Tour Highlights | Round 3 | Austin Championship | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 3 of the 2026 Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions, featuring Trace Crowe, Erik van Rooyen, Chad Ramey and Sami Valimaki, among others.

The PGA Tour returns to Austin for the inaugural Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions, with the FedExCup Fall reaching its penultimate event at Omni Barton Creek. Fresh off a historic maiden victory in Mexico, teenage sensation Blades Brown headlines the field alongside Austin Smotherman, who arrives chasing a third consecutive win after triumphs in Utah and Bermuda. Ryan Gerard, Jackson Koivun and University of Texas alumni Pierceson Coody and Doug Ghim add further quality. With 2027 Tour status and places in next season’s Signature Events still up for grabs, the battle around the FedExCup top-100 and top-60 cut-offs are reaching a crucial stage.

videos.summary_source_text:
Drivers On A Mission + McLaren v Red Bull | Las Vegas GP Preview | F1 Nation AWS - Global AI Partner of Formula 1 - sponsors this episode of F1 Nation

Tom Clarkson, Jolyon Palmer and James Hinchcliffe look ahead to F1 touching down in the Nevada desert for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, a race like no other. They're also paid a visit by McLaren's Senior Racing Director Randy Singh for an insight into how the team are approaching the final three races of the season and their focus on finishing ahead of Red Bull in the Constructors' Championship.

There's also debate around what Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur should do with his 'dream and nightmare' driver lineup of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, towards the end of the season and beyond. Also, do Aston Martin have a good base of a car to build on, after an improved showing last time out in Brazil? 

Plus, the trio react to the news that Liam Lawson has re-signed alongside Arvid Lindblad for Racing Bulls in 2027.

videos.summary_source_text:
Avalanche Leave Montreal With a Solid Win in First Game Without MacKinnon and Makar Colorado Avalanche shine without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar, toppling the Montreal Canadiens 4-1 on the road. Can the Avs maintain momentum despite missing two of their biggest stars?

The conversation focused on Mike Reilly’s arrival via waiver claim from the Carolina Hurricanes, bringing much-needed defensive depth as the Avalanche navigate their injury challenges. A key theme that emerged was Colorado’s balanced effort—Brock Nelson, Martin Nečas, Artturi Lehkonen, and others stepped up, with Mackenzie Blackwood delivering a standout .962 save percentage. The discussion explored the overturned high-stick goal, officiating transparency, and whether this gritty win signals sustained success or a brief spark. With special teams showing signs of improvement and upcoming matchups looming, can Colorado’s “next man up” mentality carry them through a tough stretch in the Western Conference?

videos.summary_source_text:
Cold Feet, Tingling Legs? Don't Ignore This Vitamin!  Dr. Mandell Cold feet, tingling legs, numbness, burning sensations, muscle weakness, and poor balance could be warning signs that your nerves and circulation need attention. Many people assume these symptoms are simply part of aging, but an overlooked vitamin deficiency could be contributing to the problem. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the important role of vitamin B12 in maintaining healthy nerves, producing red blood cells, supporting oxygen delivery throughout the body, and protecting the myelin sheath that surrounds your nerves. Discover why vitamin B12 deficiency becomes more common with age, how certain medications and dietary habits affect absorption, and why nerve problems can sometimes feel like poor circulation. You'll also learn simple, practical ways to support healthier blood flow in your legs, activate your calf muscles, improve mobility, and protect your nerve health through walking, movement, proper nutrition, and healthy lifestyle habits. Most importantly, understand the warning signs that should never be ignored and why identifying the real cause of your symptoms is essential. Your legs and feet can tell you a great deal about your overall health. Listen to what your body is telling you, take action, and share this important information with someone you care about. Make it a great day! Dr. Alan Mandell

videos.title: Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap!
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap! Elon Musk says Grok 4.8 has 2.5 TRILLION parameters, making it xAI's biggest model yet. But here's the twist: Musk himself admits it isn't as good as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. And after a nearly two-month delay, xAI still hasn't published independent benchmark results to prove what its massive engineering overhaul actually achieved.

So why did xAI throw out its existing AI software stack and rebuild it from scratch in C and C++? And can a 100,000-GPU supercomputer help Grok close the gap with OpenAI and Anthropic?

The story behind Grok 4.8 is much bigger than another AI model release.

On November 10, Musk announced that Grok 4.8 had completed pre-training and entered reinforcement learning, with a limited rollout to Grok Bot users reportedly planned. But xAI hasn't published a Grok 4.8 model card, official benchmarks, API pricing, or a confirmed public release date.

That makes the 2.5-trillion-parameter claim particularly interesting. According to Musk's figures, Grok 4.8 is approximately 19% larger than Grok 4.7 and roughly 67% larger than Grok 4.6. But bigger models don't automatically deliver better intelligence.

And xAI's own Grok 4.7 benchmark chart reveals why.

On CursorBench 4.0, Grok 4.7 scored 46.3%, compared with 41.7% for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. That's impressive until you notice Claude Fable 5.1 scored 51.8%. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, the reported gap was even larger, with Grok around 38% against Fable's 58%.

These numbers matter because Grok 4.8 isn't competing against last year's AI models. It's entering a market already occupied by Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Google's Gemini lineup.

But the most unusual part of this story is what happened behind the scenes.

Musk says xAI abandoned JAX and SGLang in favor of custom C and C++ infrastructure for reinforcement learning and inference. He also says the Starlink software team developed an internal pre-training stack using low-level optimizations targeting Nvidia GPUs.

The potential advantage? Faster training, lower overhead, and more efficient use of expensive AI hardware.

The catch? Rebuilding critical infrastructure takes time, introduces engineering risks, and doesn't guarantee better model performance. Musk previously suggested the custom stack could deliver more than a tenfold training speedup on large runs, but that projection remains independently unverified.

Meanwhile, xAI's Colossus supercomputer in Memphis represents another extraordinary investment. Its original 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPU cluster was assembled in just 122 days, while Musk has described newer infrastructure targeting 220,000 Nvidia GB300 chips.

That's an enormous amount of compute behind a model that hasn't yet demonstrated its capabilities publicly.

We also examine what 2.5 trillion parameters actually means, why mixture-of-experts architectures complicate model-size comparisons, and why total parameter counts reveal surprisingly little about real-world coding, reasoning, and agent performance.

Then there's the business question.

Grok 4.7 offers API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, making it significantly cheaper on output than several frontier competitors. If Grok 4.8 delivers substantial improvements while preserving that advantage, xAI could become an increasingly attractive option for developers building AI agents.

But if the rewrite produces another delayed model that still trails Anthropic's best, the economics become harder to defend.

We break down the confirmed information, Musk's unverified claims, the overlooked benchmark results, the software rewrite, Colossus infrastructure, and what Grok 4.8 must accomplish to justify the investment.

The real question isn't whether xAI can build a bigger AI model.

It's whether all that hardware, custom software, and additional training can produce something meaningfully better.

Subscribe to BitBiased for analytical coverage of OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, AI infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the technology shaping the future.

01:34 What xAI Has Confirmed vs. What Is Only Musk's Word
03:41 The Line in Grok 4.7's Launch Chart xAI Didn't Headline
06:39 Why xAI Deleted Its Own Software Stack
08:29 What a From-Scratch Rewrite Can Win, and What It Costs
10:26 What 2.5 Trillion Parameters Does and Doesn't Mean
12:23 The 100,000-GPU Machine Behind the Bet
14:06 Where Grok Stands Against Today's Frontier, Not Last Year's
16:31 The Verdict

videos.summary_source_text:

Laddhybrid eller elbil? Nu kommer dom på rad, den nya generationens superladdhybrider som lovar 11 till 14 mil på ren el och snabbladdning. Jag har testat tre av dom mot varandra. Leapmotor C10 EREV för 429 900 kr, Skoda Kodiaq iV för 506 400 kr och nya Toyota RAV4 Laddhybrid för 577 900 kr.

Sex ronder. Säkerhet, räckvidd och laddning, utrymmen, köra och åka, wow-känsla och ekonomi. Hur långt går dom egentligen på el? Leapmotorn klarade 118 km i vårt test. Och hur törstiga blir dom när batteriet är slut?

Men den stora frågan är en annan. Ska du ens köpa en laddhybrid? Jag har räknat på både köp och privatleasing, och jämfört med elbilarna Skoda Enyaq, Toyota bZ4X och Leapmotor C10 El. Svaret blev inte riktigt det jag trodde …

Vilken skulle du välja? Laddhybrid eller elbil? Skriv i kommentarerna!

Prenumerera gärna och bli medlem i kanalen. Det betyder jättemycket.

Kapitalkostnad 4,5 % på hela beloppet.

videos.title: Round 4 Highlights | 2026 DP World Tour Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Round 4 Highlights | 2026 DP World Tour Championship Highlights from the final round of the DP World Tour season at the DP World Tour Championship where the Race to Dubai goes down to the wire between Rory McIlroy & Eugenio Chacarra. Whilst Tyrrell Hatton aims to secure his ninth DP World Tour title at Jumeirah Golf Estates. Featuring Rory McIlroy, Tyrrell Hatton, Eugenio Chacarra, Kristoffer Reitan and more!

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. There are two key pieces of silverware on offer this week, The DP World Tour Championship and the Harry Vardon Trophy. The battle for the Race to Dubai title comes to an end this week at Jumeirah Golf Club as players vie to end the year as DP World Tour Number One. There are still nine players in the running to end the year at the top of the Ranking. Eugenio Chacarra, the only three time winner this season, tops the standings heading in with a 533.93 point lead over nearest challenger Rory McIlroy, who is seeking to match Colin Montgomerie’s long-standing record of eight Order of Merit titles this week. With Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier all are still in with a chance of ending the year as the winner of the season-long race.

The Real Cause of Tinnitus (It's Not in Your Ears) Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, involves more than just the ears themselves. The brain stem plays an important role in how these phantom sounds are perceived, especially when the inner ear isn’t receiving enough energy to function properly.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/LZNf7O4fqSc 

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47QalXT

When energy levels in the inner ear drop, the brain stem compensates by increasing its sensitivity to sound. GABA, a neurotransmitter that helps calm nerve activity, normally helps regulate this response.

Vitamin B1 is important for both energy production in the inner ear and GABA function. A deficiency can interfere with these processes and contribute to tinnitus symptoms.

Allithiamine is a form of vitamin B1 originally derived from garlic that can cross the blood-brain barrier and help support energy production and GABA activity in the brainstem.

7 Silent Signs of Pancreatic Cancer Many people don’t know they have pancreatic cancer until it’s too late. The earlier you can detect it, the better the prognosis.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️ https://youtu.be/o_Uro77TvvQ

🌟 Take Dr. Berg’s New 60-Second Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4khCLkP

Pay attention to these 7 early warning signs: https://drbrg.co/3Uw5Uyk

1. Sudden unexpected weight loss

A problem with the pancreas can affect digestion and appetite, which can cause you to lose weight unexpectedly.

2. Abdominal pain

This is typically dull, persistent pain that can radiate to the left shoulder. Sometimes, it shows up as radiating pain in the belly button that extends into the spine and often feels worse after eating.

3. Jaundice

This is characterized by yellowing of the whites of the eyes and rust-colored urine caused by bile backing up into the blood.

4. Chronic diarrhea

Most pancreatic cancer affects the part of the pancreas that is responsible for digestive enzymes, which can often lead to chronic diarrhea.

5. Diabetes

A tumor in the pancreas can disrupt the cells that produce insulin, contributing to diabetes.

6. Feeling full quickly

Pancreatic cancer can cause you to feel full and bloated, even if you’ve hardly had anything to eat.

7. Persistent fatigue

This can be described as overwhelming, chronic fatigue that doesn’t improve with more sleep.

videos.title: What Happens Inside Your Body After You Eat a Banana?  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
What Happens Inside Your Body After You Eat a Banana?  Dr. Mandell Bananas provide carbohydrates and fiber, and people can feel differently after eating one. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how digestion and food pairing can affect the body’s response, and demonstrates eating a banana with almond butter. Pairing carbohydrates with fat or protein can slow the rise in blood glucose after a meal, though each person’s response varies. A little cinnamon is optional for flavor; the video isn’t suggesting that cinnamon treats blood sugar problems.

PubMed references: I’d keep Jenkins for general background and add the almond butter study. The almond study tested several forms of almonds, including almond butter, with a carbohydrate-containing meal; it did not test bananas specifically. pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
- Jenkins DJA et al. “Glycemic index of foods: a physiological basis for carbohydrate exchange.” Am J Clin Nutr. 1981;34(3):362–366. PMID: 6259925.
- “Acute and second-meal effects of almond form in impaired glucose tolerant adults: a randomized crossover trial.” PMID: 21276226.

Challenge Ahead: Cale Makar Out At Least Two Week. Nathan MacKinnon Out At Least Four Weeks. Colorado Avalanche suffer a major blow as Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon face weeks on the sidelines. Can rising prospects like Alex Gagné and Gavin Brindley step up, or will the Avs struggle to stay afloat without their two superstars?

The conversation focused on the fallout from Makar’s projected two-week absence and MacKinnon’s four-week recovery, examining roles for Gagné alongside Brent Burns and Brindley’s offensive hot streak with the Colorado Eagles. Key topics include potential defensive pairings, power-play adjustments—especially with Devon Toews potentially quarterbacking—and whether the Avalanche’s depth can carry them through this challenging stretch. The discussion explored the Avalanche’s upcoming schedule and the opportunities this adversity presents for younger players to shine. Brady Tkachuk, Panthers Morning Skate: Blues Celebrate Keith Tkachuk in St. Louis Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks to the media before his team plays the host St. Louis Blues on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026.

The Blues will honor Keith Tkachuk tonight with Brady and Matthew part of the pregame celebration.

Florida is coming off a 5-4 comeback win against Detroit. The Panthers trailed 4-1 late in the second before Gus Forsling scored. 

The Panthers scored three goals in the third for the win — with Anton Lundell getting two of them including the game winner. 

Carter Verhaeghe had three assists with Sam Reinhart and Lars Eller also scoring.  

Florida has won two straight.

The Panthers play at St. Louis on Saturday and Dallas on Sunday.

videos.title: OpenAI’s GPT-7: A 10 Trillion Parameter Model Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s GPT-7: A 10 Trillion Parameter Model Massive Upgrade! GPT-7 could be OpenAI's biggest leap yet. But as of November 13, 2026, there's no official GPT-7 announcement, no confirmed release date, and no verified specifications. What we do have is something potentially more interesting: OpenAI has described an unnamed internal AI model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra.

Meanwhile, a mysterious leak claims OpenAI is developing a secret AI model codenamed "Bel," supposedly featuring more than 10 TRILLION parameters. Could this be GPT-7? Or is the internet connecting rumors that have no proven relationship?

Sam Altman has pointed toward AGI-level AI by the end of 2026. GPT-6 Astra launched in September with extraordinary reported benchmark results, including 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, 96% on GPQA Diamond, and a one-million-token context window. Yet major limitations remain in autonomous reasoning, long-running tasks, cybersecurity, and reliability.

And that's where the GPT-7 story gets interesting.

On September 8, OpenAI published details about an internal model reportedly capable of mathematical reasoning beyond Astra, including work related to the Navier–Stokes equations. OpenAI also disclosed a new training run beginning August 28. But the company never identified either model as GPT-7, and the mathematical claims haven't been independently verified in the research examined here.

So what's actually happening behind the scenes?

We trace the evolution from GPT-3's 175 billion parameters through GPT-4, GPT-5, and GPT-6, examining how AI evolved from generating text into writing code, operating computers, and completing increasingly complex workflows.

We break down GPT-6 Astra's reported capabilities, including its 58% Terminal-Bench coding performance, 100% ExploitBench result, and advanced reasoning abilities. Those numbers are impressive, but they also reveal why benchmark dominance doesn't automatically translate into reliable real-world autonomy.

Then we investigate the controversial Bel leak. The anonymous claim suggests an internal model exceeding 10 trillion parameters, more than 57 times GPT-3's size. But there's no verified OpenAI documentation connecting Bel, the rumored Doug project, or any alleged parameter count to GPT-7.

The stronger evidence comes from OpenAI itself: an unnamed model reportedly exceeding Astra's capabilities. That's a very different claim from confirming GPT-7.

We also explore what a genuine next-generation breakthrough could look like.

Could GPT-7 independently plan, write, test, and debug entire software projects? Could advanced self-verification reduce hallucinations and reasoning failures? Could persistent memory, real-time voice, video understanding, and computer control transform ChatGPT into an AI agent capable of managing complete workdays?

OpenAI claims its researchers already receive approximately 3.1 agent-workdays of output per human workday. But that internal productivity figure doesn't prove a future model can operate reliably without supervision.

And the competition is accelerating. Google's Gemini 3.8, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, xAI's Grok 4.6, and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 all form part of the increasingly competitive AI landscape.

Beyond raw intelligence, the biggest questions concern AGI, cybersecurity, prompt injection, autonomous decision-making, privacy, and the economic consequences of AI systems capable of performing increasingly valuable work.

Could GPT-7 finally qualify as artificial general intelligence? Would it represent a revolutionary architectural breakthrough or another incremental improvement? And could its release arrive in 2027, 2028, or somewhere entirely unexpected?

Throughout this investigation, we separate confirmed developments, OpenAI's own claims, unverified leaks, and informed predictions.

Because the real question isn't whether GPT-7 will score higher on benchmarks.

It's whether OpenAI can build an AI system you can trust to finish complex work without constantly watching it.

videos.title: Jensen Huang's Scandal & The Truth!
videos.summary_source_text:
Jensen Huang's Scandal & The Truth! Jensen Huang's reported resignation from Nvidia has sparked a wave of explosive claims involving four women, alleged affairs, a suspected Chinese spy, and a potential national security scandal. But how much of the Jensen Huang controversy is actually supported by evidence?

From Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, an unnamed employee, and Jensen Huang's wife Lori Huang, the stories circulating online range from documented facts to anonymous allegations. And some of the most serious accusations have the least publicly available proof.

This video breaks down every woman linked to Jensen Huang, separating confirmed facts, credible reporting, and unverified allegations using Nvidia statements, SEC filings, reported accounts from Reuters and The New York Times, and Huang's reported apology letter.

**KIMBERLY POWELL — THE NVIDIA EXECUTIVE**

Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, reportedly had an extramarital relationship with Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times, citing five current and former employees. The allegations raise questions about Nvidia's corporate code of conduct, executive accountability, and relationships involving direct reports.

But neither Powell nor Huang has publicly confirmed the reported relationship. What does the evidence actually establish?

**ALICE HUANG — THE ALLEGED CHINESE SPY**

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman associated with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner.

According to the script's account of reporting from The New York Times, U.S. intelligence officials suspected she was connected to Chinese intelligence and efforts to redirect Nvidia technology toward China.

But the alleged intelligence memo remains confidential, no charges have been filed, and China has rejected the accusations. Nvidia's board reportedly stated it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

Photographs of Alice Huang with Jensen Huang at industry events do not establish espionage or a romantic relationship.

So why has this allegation become such a major part of the controversy?

**THE UNNAMED NVIDIA EMPLOYEE**

Reuters reportedly identified another alleged relationship involving an unnamed Nvidia employee, citing two anonymous sources.

No identity, photographs, or public documentary confirmation have emerged. We examine why credible reporting and confirmed facts are not interchangeable.

**LORI HUANG — JENSEN HUANG'S WIFE**

Lori Huang, formerly Lori Mills, met Jensen Huang while studying electrical engineering at Oregon State University. They married in 1985 and have supported major educational and AI research initiatives, including a $50 million gift to Oregon State.

The script describes a letter in which Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful and apologized for hurting his wife and family.

But has Lori Huang spoken publicly? Is there evidence supporting online divorce rumors? And what can actually be established about their marriage?

**NVIDIA INVESTIGATION, STOCK LOSSES, AND WHAT COMES NEXT**

The reported scandal also raises larger questions about Nvidia's leadership, corporate governance, AI chip exports, and U.S.-China technology competition.

We examine the reported independent investigation involving Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor Joon Kim, congressional interest in Nvidia's China business, and reports of a roughly $1.8 trillion decline in Nvidia's market value from its October peak.

Importantly, Nvidia's share-price movements cannot automatically be attributed entirely to the controversy. AI regulation, semiconductor market conditions, and broader investor concerns also matter.

By the end, you'll understand which relationships are documented, which allegations come from reputable reporting, which claims remain unverified, and what evidence would be needed to resolve the biggest unanswered questions.

This breakdown reflects the claims and reporting described in the script as of November 14, 2026. Allegations are not findings of wrongdoing, and the claims discussed should not be treated as independently verified.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Jensen Huang Scandal: What's Actually True?

#JensenHuang #Nvidia #KimberlyPowell #AliceHuang #NvidiaNews Jensen Huang's reported resignation from Nvidia has sparked a wave of explosive claims involving four women, alleged affairs, a suspected Chinese spy, and a potential national security scandal. But how much of the Jensen Huang controversy is actually supported by evidence?

From Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, an unnamed employee, and Jensen Huang's wife Lori Huang, the stories circulating online range from documented facts to anonymous allegations. And some of the most serious accusations have the least publicly available proof.

This video breaks down every woman linked to Jensen Huang, separating confirmed facts, credible reporting, and unverified allegations using Nvidia statements, SEC filings, reported accounts from Reuters and The New York Times, and Huang's reported apology letter.

**KIMBERLY POWELL — THE NVIDIA EXECUTIVE**

Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, reportedly had an extramarital relationship with Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times, citing five current and former employees. The allegations raise questions about Nvidia's corporate code of conduct, executive accountability, and relationships involving direct reports.

But neither Powell nor Huang has publicly confirmed the reported relationship. What does the evidence actually establish?

**ALICE HUANG — THE ALLEGED CHINESE SPY**

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman associated with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner.

According to the script's account of reporting from The New York Times, U.S. intelligence officials suspected she was connected to Chinese intelligence and efforts to redirect Nvidia technology toward China.

But the alleged intelligence memo remains confidential, no charges have been filed, and China has rejected the accusations. Nvidia's board reportedly stated it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

Photographs of Alice Huang with Jensen Huang at industry events do not establish espionage or a romantic relationship.

So why has this allegation become such a major part of the controversy?

**THE UNNAMED NVIDIA EMPLOYEE**

Reuters reportedly identified another alleged relationship involving an unnamed Nvidia employee, citing two anonymous sources.

No identity, photographs, or public documentary confirmation have emerged. We examine why credible reporting and confirmed facts are not interchangeable.

**LORI HUANG — JENSEN HUANG'S WIFE**

Lori Huang, formerly Lori Mills, met Jensen Huang while studying electrical engineering at Oregon State University. They married in 1985 and have supported major educational and AI research initiatives, including a $50 million gift to Oregon State.

The script describes a letter in which Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful and apologized for hurting his wife and family.

But has Lori Huang spoken publicly? Is there evidence supporting online divorce rumors? And what can actually be established about their marriage?

**NVIDIA INVESTIGATION, STOCK LOSSES, AND WHAT COMES NEXT**

The reported scandal also raises larger questions about Nvidia's leadership, corporate governance, AI chip exports, and U.S.-China technology competition.

We examine the reported independent investigation involving Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor Joon Kim, congressional interest in Nvidia's China business, and reports of a roughly $1.8 trillion decline in Nvidia's market value from its October peak.

Importantly, Nvidia's share-price movements cannot automatically be attributed entirely to the controversy. AI regulation, semiconductor market conditions, and broader investor concerns also matter.

By the end, you'll understand which relationships are documented, which allegations come from reputable reporting, which claims remain unverified, and what evidence would be needed to resolve the biggest unanswered questions.

This breakdown reflects the claims and reporting described in the script as of November 14, 2026. Allegations are not findings of wrongdoing, and the claims discussed should not be treated as independently verified.

videos.title: Once You Learn This Move, Bunker Shots Feel Effortless
videos.summary_source_text:
Once You Learn This Move, Bunker Shots Feel Effortless Struggle to get out of bunkers consistently, hit bunker shots thin or leave the ball in the sand?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn a simple bunker shot concept that can make greenside bunker play feel much easier and help you get the ball out more consistently.

The key is not trying to scoop the golf ball into the air.

Instead, Danny Maude shows you how to **push sand into the back of the golf ball** and use that sand to carry the ball out of the bunker.

This simple visual helped one of Danny’s students get out first time, and it can also help you control your strike, the depth of sand you take and the height of the shot.

In this golf lesson you’ll learn:

• How to stop thinning bunker shots into the face  
• Why taking too much sand kills bunker distance  
• Where the club should enter the sand  
• Why good bunker players start with the clubface open  
• How the clubface can square through impact  
• Why trying to add loft can create fat and thin bunker shots  
• How to use the sand to lift the golf ball  
• How to play bunker shots from hard compact sand  
• How to adjust for soft or fluffy sand  
• Why the swing should be fuller than most golfers realise  
• How to make bunker shots feel more relaxed and repeatable  

One of the biggest mistakes golfers make in bunkers is trying to lift the ball into the air.

That can cause the club to work backwards, the handle to stall and the strike to become inconsistent.

A much simpler picture is to focus on the sand.

Let the club enter roughly two or three inches behind the golf ball and then keep the sand moving forwards into the back of it.

When you do that, your body can begin to organise itself around the task naturally.

Most people are told there’s nothing they can do about a high calcium score on their CAC test, but that may not be true.

There are two types of arterial plaque: hard plaque and soft plaque. Your arteries are lined with a thin layer of cells called the endothelial layer. Damage and inflammation in this layer can create gaps that allow small, dense LDL particles to enter the arterial wall and contribute to arterial plaque buildup.

High blood glucose, high blood pressure, and low vitamin D can contribute to arterial damage. The endothelial layer contains numerous vitamin D receptors, and vitamin D supports nitric oxide production, helping blood vessels relax and improve circulation.

Vitamin K2 helps direct calcium toward the bones rather than the arteries. Together, magnesium, vitamin D3, and vitamin K2 support endothelial health and healthy blood vessels.

It’s America vs Italy in this quarter-mile drag race! 🇺🇸🇮🇹

Mat’s lining up against the brand-new, twin-turbo hybrid Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X in the legendary plug-in hybrid Ferrari SF90 Stradale. On paper, this is an absolute heavyweight clash of hybrid hypercars - so let’s see how the stats stack up before they hit the runway!

Starting with the Chevy, the Corvette ZR1X pairs a ferocious 5.5-litre twin-turbo flat-plane crank V8 with a front-mounted electric motor to produce a staggering 1,267hp and 1,123Nm of torque! Power is sent to all four wheels and it has an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox. The whole thing tips the scales at 1,875kg and it costs $240,995

Then we have the Ferrari SF90 Stradale. Behind the driver sits a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, assisted by three electric motors for a combined output of 1,000hp and 800Nm of torque. Like the Corvette, it sends power to all four wheels through and also has an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. Though it has a slight weight advantage, coming in at 1,670kg and it costs around $540,489

With 267hp more in the Chevy, you might think the ZR1X has this in the bag—but Ferrari’s launch control and lighter kerb weight make it a serious giant-killer! Will American muscle take the crown, or will Italian engineering hold the line? There’s only one way to find out… LET’S RACE! 🏁

videos.summary_source_text:
13.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.title: The 90-Year Race to Reverse Aging (Documentary)
videos.summary_source_text:
The 90-Year Race to Reverse Aging (Documentary) Aging is the price we pay for being alive, but a growing number of scientists think it may not always be this way. This documentary follows the 90-year race to slow and reverse human aging. It runs from Clive McCay's underfed rats in the 1930s, through the rise and fall of the "red wine molecule" and the drug discovered in Easter Island soil, to Bryan Johnson's $2-million-a-year experiment on himself and the first human trial of cell "reprogramming" in 2026. Then we ask what actually works in people today.

videos.title: NVIDIA's $4 Trillion Empire Is Shaking — The Jensen Huang Scandal Explained
videos.summary_source_text:
NVIDIA's $4 Trillion Empire Is Shaking — The Jensen Huang Scandal Explained Nvidia's board publicly backed Jensen Huang on Sunday. By Thursday, the CEO who built a $4.5 trillion AI chip empire was gone — effective immediately. And at the center of the controversy is an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, billions of dollars in GPU deals, and a relationship that has raised serious national security questions.

Did a Chinese spy really bring down Nvidia's legendary CEO? Or is the story far more complicated than the headlines suggest?

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent 33 years turning a graphics chip company into the backbone of the global AI industry. From ChatGPT and AI data centers to the world's most advanced GPU infrastructure, Nvidia became one of the most valuable companies on Earth. But its success was also closely tied to one man.

Then came reports involving Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former television reporter and executive at Singapore-based GPU company Megaspeed. According to The New York Times, US officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset. The Financial Times reported additional allegations involving China's Ministry of State Security and a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang. Those espionage allegations remain unproven, and Alice Huang has not been charged.

The business connections make this story even more consequential.

Megaspeed reportedly purchased billions of dollars in Nvidia AI equipment through its Southeast Asian operations. Its assets reportedly grew from roughly $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024. Trade records cited by The New York Times suggested at least $4.8 billion in AI equipment purchases, while Bloomberg estimated approximately $4.6 billion and 136,000 GPUs.

Why does that matter? US export controls restrict China's access to Nvidia's most advanced AI chips. But renting GPU computing power from data centers outside China can be legal. That distinction creates a complicated question about AI chip exports, Singapore, Malaysia, Alibaba, and whether hardware was diverted to China.

Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. Nvidia says it complies with export regulations. And the more explosive claims — including a reported $7.5 billion in shipments allegedly enabled by the relationship — have not been established as fact.

Meanwhile, the corporate timeline is extraordinary.

On November 8, Jensen Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation while publicly expressing confidence in him. Days later, reports of additional relationships and potential board action emerged. By Thursday, Nvidia announced Huang's immediate resignation as CEO, president, and director, without publicly stating a reason.

The market reaction was brutal. Nvidia shares fell as much as 8.8% on Monday, wiping out roughly $192 billion in market value. Following the resignation announcement, shares plunged more than 13% in early Thursday trading before recovering some losses. Nvidia's valuation temporarily slipped below $4 trillion, behind Apple and Microsoft.

Now CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, Harvey Jones has become board chair, and investors are watching Nvidia's next earnings report, the independent investigation, possible export-control enforcement, and congressional scrutiny.

This video separates confirmed events from anonymous-source reporting and unproven intelligence allegations. We examine the Megaspeed GPU business, the AI chip rental loophole, the board's sudden reversal, Nvidia's stock reaction, and what Jensen Huang's departure could mean for the AI industry.

The biggest unanswered question isn't simply whether Jensen Huang was targeted by intelligence operatives. It's whether any national security compromise occurred — and why Nvidia's board changed course so quickly.

videos.title: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen Is INSANE — AI Agents Just Leveled Up!
videos.summary_source_text:
Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen Is INSANE — AI Agents Just Leveled Up! Google just released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its third Gemini 4 model in just 43 days. And here's the surprising part: Google's newest, smallest, fastest model scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching the 50-point performance of Gemini 4 Argon, the flagship Google released just a month earlier.

But Hydrogen isn't trying to beat Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's most powerful model. It's part of a bigger strategy that could change how AI agents work, how developers build software, and how much businesses pay for AI.

Google claims Hydrogen runs 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, dramatically reduces hallucinations, and delivers a major improvement in agentic coding. On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Google reports a jump from 18.2% to 57%. Hydrogen also supports a massive 1-million-token context window, multimodal understanding, and four thinking levels, including the new xhigh mode.

But do the independent benchmarks support Google's claims?

We examine Hydrogen's performance against Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 4 Carbon. At xhigh, Hydrogen reaches 54 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, just one point behind Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol at their maximum settings. Yet the results become much more complicated when you look at coding, terminal tasks, computer use, and real-world agent reliability.

Google's demos are equally ambitious. Hydrogen builds an interactive Minecraft-style voxel island, turns Google Sheets into animated pixel art, creates a complex e-commerce storefront with WebGL2 graphics, generates and audits Google Slides presentations, builds financial models, and assembles a video using existing footage and specialized tools.

These aren't just chatbot demonstrations. They're examples of AI systems writing code, executing tasks, inspecting results, and correcting their own mistakes.

And that's where the real story begins.

Google also introduced Orchestrator inside Google Antigravity, combining Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen in a single agent workflow. Carbon handles complex reasoning, exploration, and planning, while Hydrogen executes code changes, updates packages, and runs tests.

Google claims this combination achieves near-Carbon performance while using 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster. But those figures come from Google's own testing, and independent verification remains limited.

Could this planner-and-executor architecture be more important than Hydrogen itself?

We also break down the pricing. Hydrogen costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with cached input available for just $0.075 per million tokens. That's cheaper than Google's frontier models, but twice the current price of Gemini 3.8 Flash and more expensive per token than OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra.

And there's another catch: Hydrogen's default high thinking level can significantly affect the actual cost of completing a task. Faster inference doesn't automatically mean cheaper workflows.

Hydrogen is already available through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Android Studio, Google Search, and other Google products. But access to Orchestrator is more restricted, and free Gemini users won't necessarily get Hydrogen for every prompt.

We examine where Hydrogen genuinely excels, where Carbon and Claude still outperform it, why Google's own demonstrations deserve scrutiny, and what the rapid release of three Gemini 4 models tells us about the next phase of AI competition.

Is Gemini 4 Hydrogen a genuine breakthrough in AI intelligence? Or is Google proving that the future belongs to smaller, faster models working alongside more powerful reasoning systems?

The answer could matter more than another benchmark victory.

Gus Forsling Turns Momentum Around, Panthers Rally from down 4-1 to Beat Red Wings Florida Panthers defenseman Gus Forsling speaks to the media after his team rallied to beat the visiting Detroit Red Wings 5-4 on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, in Sunrise.

The Panthers trailed 4-1 late in the second before Gus Forsling scored. 

Florida scored three goals in the third for the win — with Anton Lundell getting two of them including the game winner. 

Carter Verhaeghe had three assists with Sam Reinhart and Lars Eller also scoring.  

Florida has won two straight; Detroit has lost five in a row. 

The Panthers play at St. Louis on Saturday and Dallas on Sunday.

videos.title: Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check
videos.summary_source_text:
Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check If you’re fighting a slice, check your clubface at 9 o’clock and 3 o’clock.
At 9 o’clock, you don’t want the face hanging wide open. Then as you swing through to 3 o’clock, let the club rotate naturally while the path works slightly out to the right.

A lot of golfers try to fix a slice by just swinging farther right, but if the face is still open, the ball is still going right.

Get the face and path working together and you can start turning that slice into a draw.
The Blue Brick makes this easy to practice because it gives you something to swing around. Set it down, let the club work through its natural arc, and miss the brick on the way through.

Want an easy way to work on your club path without thinking about a bunch of positions?
Use the Blue Brick as your reference and practice swinging around it. It gives you instant feedback if your path starts getting off.

videos.title: Legal… But Should It Be? The Vice Neon Sunset Problem
videos.summary_source_text:
Legal… But Should It Be? The Vice Neon Sunset Problem Does your golf ball's paint change where it goes? We tested the two-tone Vice Neon Sunset on the robot, and turning it around moved it about 8.5 yards.

📰 TaylorMade sues Callaway over "mud ball" paint claims: https://mygolfspy.com/news-opinion/taylormade-sues-callaway-over-chrome-tour-claims-alleging-false-advertising-and-a-mud-ball-campaign/
🧪 We tested the Polara anti-slice ball: https://mygolfspy.com/labs/polara-golf-ball-test-mygolfspy/

Tony Covey and Andrew Zanzig dig into the USGA's symmetry rule, written in 1981 to stop the Polara, and why a ball can pass as written but still not pass the spirit of the rule. Teed one way, the Neon Sunset faded. Flipped, 11 of 12 balls drew. It's still on the USGA's conforming list. Should it be?

17:14 Robot test: What the Neon Sunset did

33:16 Letter vs. spirit of the rule
43:20 What it means for golfers
50:07 Should Vice conform?

videos.title: Best Home Ab Workout // Just 10 Min // 6 PACK GUARANTEED!
videos.summary_source_text:
Best Home Ab Workout // Just 10 Min // 6 PACK GUARANTEED! If you are looking for the best home ab workout you can do without any equipment, this 10 minute follow along routine is a great place to start. In this video, I’m going to take you through seven bodyweight ab exercises that you can do in the comfort of your own home, whether you are a beginner or an experienced lifter.

Get a flat stomach here - https://athleanx.com/flatstomach
Subscribe to this channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

The key to a successful home abs workout is keeping it simple enough to do consistently while making sure the exercises challenge your core. You don’t need an ab machine, a set of dumbbells or a gym membership. Every exercise in this routine uses your own bodyweight, and all you need is enough floor space to move comfortably.

The structure of the ab workout is simple.

There are 7 exercises, each performed for 60 seconds. If you are a beginner and cannot make it through the entire minute, perform the exercise for as long as you can with good form. Take a brief break when needed and rejoin the workout when you are ready. Your goal is to gradually build up the strength and endurance to complete more of each interval without sacrificing the quality of your reps.

Some of the exercises are divided into 30 seconds on each side or in each direction. These changes are noted below and demonstrated in the video so you can follow along without stopping to figure out what comes next.

Between exercises, you will get 30 seconds to rest. During that time, I’ll explain the next movement and show you how to perform it. This makes the routine easy to save and come back to whenever you want an ab workout at home that takes the guesswork out of your training.

Here is how the workout breaks down:

1. Ab Halos - 30 seconds clockwise / 30 seconds counterclockwise | 30 seconds rest
2. Frog Crunches - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
3. Russian Rows - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
4. Thread the Needle - 30 seconds each side | 30 seconds rest
5. Black Widow Knee Slides - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
6. Frog Circles - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
7. Sliding Ab Tucks - 60 seconds

Remember, the goal is not to rush through as many reps as possible just to keep moving for the full minute. Focus on controlling each rep and making your abs do the work. A shorter interval performed well gives you a better starting point than forcing yourself through an exercise after you have lost control of the movement.

What makes this home ab workout effective is the variety of ways you are challenging your core. Instead of repeating the same crunch over and over, you will work through movements that involve curling, rotation and maintaining control of your trunk as your arms and legs move. Pay attention to the demonstrations so you understand what each exercise should look like before your next interval begins.

One of the problems with many ab workouts is that people focus on moving their legs without paying attention to what their pelvis and lower back are doing. Your hip flexors naturally contribute to certain movements, but simply swinging your legs through a rep is not the same thing as deliberately training your abs.

Watch the position of your body, control the movement and follow the form cues throughout the video. If you can no longer maintain that control, pause and reset. Don’t assume that making an exercise faster or forcing a bigger range of motion will make it a better ab exercise.

People often ask how often they should train their abs. The first step is finding a routine you can perform consistently and recover from. Having a short, no equipment ab workout ready to go makes that easier. You can fit it around your regular workouts or do it at home when getting to the gym is not an option.

As you improve, use the same routine to measure your progress. Can you complete more of the interval with clean reps? Can you take fewer breaks without rushing? Can you maintain better control from the first exercise to the last? Those are useful signs that your core strength and endurance are improving.

Of course, building your abs and revealing your abs are two parts of the same goal. This workout can help you train your abdominal muscles, but getting visible six pack abs also depends on your overall body fat levels. Pair your training with a consistent approach to nutrition instead of expecting an ab workout alone to reveal your six pack.

videos.title: Därför är nya BMW i3 BMW:s viktigaste! Podd: Varför? Därför!
videos.summary_source_text:
Därför är nya BMW i3 BMW:s viktigaste! Podd: Varför? Därför! Nya BMW i3 går 90 mil på en laddning och laddar 40 mil på tio minuter. Men är den verkligen BMW:s viktigaste bil?

I det här avsnittet av Bilpodden Varför? Därför! sitter Felix och jag i nya i3 på slingriga vägar utanför Marseille. Vi pratar om varför 3-serien är så central för BMW och om gamla lilla i3:an, citybilen i kolfiber som fortfarande ser modern ut. Och om hur BMW kan bygga en elbil och en bensinbil som ser likadana ut men inte delar en enda karosspanel.

Vi går igenom 40:an mot 50:an, cylindriska battericeller, 400 kW laddning och Heart of Joy, datorn som ska stå för körglädjen. Sen kör vi. Hur känns styrningen? Bromsarna? Och körassistenten, som tar oss ut på motorvägen utan händer på ratten. Vi tittar också på Panoramic iDrive, baksätet (aj) och hur i3 står sig mot Mercedes CLA, Zeekr 7GT och Tesla Model 3.

Svaret på frågan i rubriken? Kanske inte det du tror. Men den bästa 3-serien någonsin? Där är vi rätt överens.

videos.summary_source_text:
How a +4 Handicap Golfer Plays a Championship Golf Course Can Mark Crossfield break par on one of Portugal's toughest golf courses, featuring an incredible 670-yard par 5?

Join Mark, a plus-handicap golfer with ambitions of qualifying for the Legends Tour, as he tackles the stunning Amendoeira Faldo Course in the Algarve, Portugal. With enormous elevation changes, deep bunkers, challenging greens and some seriously long holes, this brutally difficult championship golf course is designed to test every aspect of his game.

Currently playing off a +2.7 handicap according to Arccos Golf, Mark is working towards becoming a +4 handicap golfer. But can he shoot under par on a golf course this demanding?

Throughout this 18-hole golf vlog, Mark puts his ball striking, short game, putting and golf course management to the test, demonstrating the decisions and techniques that can make the difference between shooting low scores and letting a promising round slip away.

Will smart golf course strategy and consistent ball striking be enough to conquer the Faldo Course?

Let us know in the comments how you think Mark's game is progressing towards his Legends Tour ambitions.
